_comment: cargo-geiger baseline (T1174): total unsafe items/expressions summed over workspace crates (used + unused). CI fails when the total grows; lower it when unsafe is removed. NOTE: cargo-geiger folds dependency unsafe into the binary package's entry, so the tool's total is clj-rt 110 + clj-aot 11 + clojure-rs rollup 121 = 242 (R1 finding 2); own-counts are unchanged. T1192 D-argv adds the clj-rt +21 (rt_argv shim + its FFI-boundary tests; the rollup folds the same +21). T73 item 8 adds +24 (rt_keyword shim + its FFI-boundary tests: clj-rt +12, rollup +12). Gap-124 slice 1 adds +10 (tools_deps_config env-mutating tests: set_var/remove_var are unsafe in edition 2024). Gap-121 slice 1 adds +10 measured (jit.rs EE surface: the unsafe C entry type plus the entry-lookup-and-call block; clj-aot 11->16, rollup folds the same +5. Both constructs are inherent to in-process MCJIT — the entry must be named as an unsafe C fn type and called — so the ratchet moves with justification rather than the code shrinking. Supersedes the +2 estimate, which undercounted the measured clj-aot growth). Gap-124 slice 3 adds +6 measured (tools_deps_api serial hermetic test: env save/restore + guard around CLJ_CONFIG, same shape as the baselined slice-1 helpers — serial, guard-restored, SAFETY-commented. In-process env control has no safe spelling in edition 2024 and the hermeticity is load-bearing, so the ratchet moves with justification like slice 1 rather than the test weakening). Gap-214 slices A/B/D land net -4 measured (268->264: clj-rt 110->112 for the fast-path shims, i64 trio, and boundary helpers; clj-eval 8->4 via consolidated env-test helpers; the clojure-rs rollup folds both. New surface minimized in review (safe workers over owned values pinned by safe unit tests plus one boundary test per shim; every prims.rs boundary call through one shared block) and offset by the same safe-worker extraction across the pre-existing clj-rt boundary. The residue is shims-by-construction (per-shim takes/borrows plus dispatch must stay in unsafe scope -- safe signatures over raw box traffic would be unsound, macro or inline hiding would game the counter).) H2H transient spinlock adds +24 measured (264->288: clj-value +12 for the TransientLock UnsafeCell spinlock replacing std Mutex, rollup folds the same +12). Transients are thread-confined by spec; the lock is a textbook Acquire/Release spinlock whose guard is the only data access. Measured: transient nth -13%, assoc! -10%, count -53% (with the VM count arm) in instructions retired. No safe spelling exists for a non-OS lock, so the ratchet moves with justification like prior slices. Issue #256 S1 (mixed AOT builds) adds +54 measured (288->342: clj-rt 112->136 for the rt_register_native/rt_run_program shims, the trampoline-result reclaim in mixed.rs, and their FFI-boundary tests (tests/mixed.rs + the mixed.rs unit trampolines); clj-aot 16->19 for the in-bounds GEP that loads trampoline args; the clojure-rs rollup folds both, +27). Minimized in review: the argv walk is shared with rt_argv (one argv_entries helper), the GEP block holds only the build_gep call, and every other mixed-runtime line is safe Rust over owned values. Calling native code and handing boxes across the C ABI has no safe spelling, so the ratchet moves with justification like prior slices. Issue #258 adds +4 measured (342->346: the single ActiveScope reborrow in clj-rt runtime::call_prim (+2) and the clojure-rs rollup folding it (+2)); sharing the program's evaluator with the prim shims needs one raw-pointer reborrow of the &mut Evaluator the interpreter hands the native-call wrapper, which removes a whole second interpreter boot per mixed binary.
